十二弦吉他以六條主弦配六條副弦，分成六個雙弦組；演奏時每組兩條弦通常一起按壓與撥: The twelve-string guitar pairs six main strings with six secondary strings, making six double courses; in playing, the two strings of a course are usually stopped and plucked together, and the note positions, chords and technique of the six-string guitar still apply. Begin with the tuning arrangement: the lower four courses are mostly in octaves and the upper two in unison; on a downward strum the higher string is usually struck first, though some electric models reverse this. Advanced picking and bending are harder, because two strings must be controlled at once. To simplify a bass line you can remove the higher octave string of the lower three courses and keep the treble strings for full strums.
十二弦吉他可追溯至十九世紀，前身包括十八世紀末六組雙弦的巴洛克吉他與十九世紀西班: The twelve-string guitar can be traced to the 19th century; its forerunners include the Baroque guitar with six double courses of the late 18th century and the Spanish double-strung guitar of the 19th. In the 1920s and 1930s it entered blues and folk, its greater volume suiting a singer accompanying themselves; in the 1930s Lydia Mendoza made it popular in Mexican-American music, and in the 1950s Fred Gerlach brought it into the American folk scene. In the 1960s the electric form became common in pop and rock: the Rickenbacker 360 became widely known through the Beatles' recordings, and the Byrds built their folk-rock sound on it. After the 1970s double-neck guitars made switching easy on stage, and the post-punk era saw a revival.
十二弦吉他常見於美國民謠、藍調、搖滾、爵士與流行音樂，原聲與電吉他皆有，早期多作: The twelve-string guitar is common in American folk, blues, rock, jazz and pop, in both acoustic and electric form. Early on it mostly accompanied a singer playing alone, and later it entered the studio and band line-ups, with solo performance too. From the 1960s it became a common electric guitar in pop and rock recording, and it appears in folk rock, progressive rock, hard rock, jazz fusion and the alternative rock, pop and indie music of the post-punk era. A double-neck electric guitar can carry a six-string and a twelve-string neck at once, which makes changing sound easy on stage.
十二弦吉他擁有醇厚溫潤的音色，音量較標準六弦吉他更加響亮宏大。其獨特之處在於每根: The twelve-string guitar has a mellow, warm timbre, louder and grander than a standard six-string. What sets it apart is that every main string has a secondary string, which makes a natural, rich choral effect and gives the sound layers and depth. The two strings of a course vibrate at slightly different frequencies, producing a bright, lustrous quality, as though several guitars were sounding at once. In range, the treble strings usually sit an octave above the bass strings, which makes for a wide spread. Next to a single-strung guitar the twelve-string is fuller and heavier, with a resonance as deep as a harp or a piano, so it carries well in a band and is often used for folk, rock and similar styles.

The neck is wide, and there are acoustic and electric forms, the acoustic being more common. You can use the note names, chords and technique of the six-string guitar, but the doubled strings make advanced technique harder. Its timbre is thicker and more resonant, and the phase difference between the paired strings produces a choral effect. In the 1920s and 30s it often accompanied blues and folk singers.

十二弦吉他琴體採用雲杉或玫瑰木等優質木材製成音板，背板與側板通常使用印度玫瑰木或: The body of the twelve-string guitar uses good timber such as spruce or rosewood for the soundboard, while the back and sides are usually Indian rosewood or Honduras mahogany to strengthen the resonance. The neck is made of mahogany or cedar, for stability and tone. The fretboard is ebony or rosewood. The twelve steel strings are made of high-carbon steel, and the bridge pins are mostly ebony or plastic. Metal parts such as the machine heads, bridge and pickguard are made of nickel silver or nickel-plated steel.
